content.text: {"title":"It's Dangerous, So Better Sign This: One Token's Round Trip","premise":"A web app wants to hand a user's identity — `{\"id\": 5, \"name\": \"itsdangerous\"}` — to a browser and get it back later without a database lookup. The browser is untrusted: it can read, edit, and replay anything it holds. ItsDangerous' job is narrow and worth stating precisely: it makes tampering detectable, not data secret. This story follows that one dict out through `URLSafeSerializer.dumps` into a token, back in through `loads`, and then follows a forged copy of the same token to the exact line where it is rejected.","chapters":[{"n":1,"title":"Two Strings Become a Trust Boundary","trace_lines":[1,1],"data_in":"URLSafeSerializer(\"secret key\", \"auth\") — a secret key and a salt, both str","data_out":"a configured serializer: secret_keys=[b'secret key'], salt=b'auth', serializer=_CompactJSON, signer=Signer, signer_kwargs={}, fallback_signers=[], is_text_serializer=True","code":["src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:190-241","src/itsdangerous/signer.py:67-73","src/itsdangerous/encoding.py:11-17","src/itsdangerous/url_safe.py:15-21","src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:33-37"],"inputs":["secret_key=\"secret key\"","salt=\"auth\""],"characters":["URLSafeSerializer","URLSafeSerializerMixin","Serializer.__init__","_make_keys_list","want_bytes","_CompactJSON","is_text_serializer"],"facts":["`_make_keys_list` accepts either a single str/bytes key or an iterable of keys; a single key becomes a one-element list, so the key-rotation path and the single-key path are the same code from here on.","The secret key is used verbatim as HMAC key material after `want_bytes`; there is no stretching or KDF, which is why the docs insist on a long random value rather than a password.","`salt` defaults to `b\"itsdangerous\"` on `Serializer`; passing `\"auth\"` replaces it. Passing `None` is allowed and defers to `Signer`'s own default `b\"itsdangerous.Signer\"`.","`URLSafeSerializerMixin.default_serializer` is `_CompactJSON`, not stdlib `json`: it sets `ensure_ascii=False` and `separators=(\",\", \":\")`, so payloads are smaller but the content is plain JSON.","`is_text_serializer` is decided once at construction by actually calling `serializer.dumps({})` and checking for `str`; that single boolean later decides whether `dumps` returns str and whether `load_payload` decodes UTF-8 first.","`default_fallback_signers` is an empty list as of 2.0 (the SHA-512 fallback was removed), so by default exactly one signer configuration is tried when unsigning."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q1.1","question":"The salt is not secret and is sitting in the source. What does it actually buy?"},{"id":"q1.2","question":"Nothing here mentions encryption. Will the user's id and name be readable by whoever holds the token?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":2,"title":"JSON, a Compression Gamble, and Base64","trace_lines":[1,1],"data_in":"{'id': 5, 'name': 'itsdangerous'}","data_out":"b'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9' (uncompressed, so no leading dot)","code":["src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:309-320","src/itsdangerous/url_safe.py:55-69","src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:271-276","src/itsdangerous/encoding.py:20-25","src/itsdangerous/_json.py:14-18"],"inputs":["obj={'id': 5, 'name': 'itsdangerous'}"],"characters":["Serializer.dumps","URLSafeSerializerMixin.dump_payload","Serializer.dump_payload","_CompactJSON.dumps","zlib.compress","base64_encode"],"facts":["`dump_payload` always compresses first and then keeps the compressed form only if it is at least two bytes shorter (`len(compressed) < len(json) - 1`); for this 37-byte JSON it is not, so the raw JSON is kept.","When compression does win, the payload is marked by a single leading `b\".\"` — an in-band flag that costs the one byte the length test reserves.","`base64_encode` uses `base64.urlsafe_b64encode` and strips `=` padding, which is what makes the token safe in URLs and cookies; the payload is encoded, not encrypted.","The compression decision is made on attacker-visible output length, so payload size leaks information about payload content — relevant if a token ever carries a secret alongside a guessable value.","`serializer_kwargs` (empty here) are passed through to `serializer.dumps`, which is the supported hook for changing JSON behaviour without subclassing."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q2.1","question":"If a compressed payload is just a dot plus base64, what stops a client from prepending a dot to force a decompression of hostile data?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q1.2","answer":"Readable by anyone. The payload is compact JSON, base64url-encoded with padding stripped — a reversible transform with no key involved. The guarantee is integrity and authenticity, never confidentiality."}]},{"n":3,"title":"Deriving the Key the Token Will Be Judged By","trace_lines":[1,1],"data_in":"b'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9' plus salt=b'auth' and secret_keys=[b'secret key']","data_out":"a 20-byte derived key = sha1(b'auth' + b'signer' + b'secret key').digest(), held inside the HMAC","code":["src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:278-285","src/itsdangerous/signer.py:129-173","src/itsdangerous/signer.py:182-213","src/itsdangerous/signer.py:215-220","src/itsdangerous/signer.py:40-64"],"inputs":["salt=None (falls back to self.salt = b'auth')","secret_keys=[b'secret key']"],"characters":["Serializer.make_signer","Signer.__init__","Signer.derive_key","Signer.get_signature","HMACAlgorithm","_lazy_sha1"],"facts":["`make_signer` signs with `self.secret_keys` (the whole list) but `derive_key()` with no argument uses `self.secret_keys[-1]` — the newest key always signs.","The default `key_derivation` is `\"django-concat\"`: `digest_method(salt + b\"signer\" + secret_key).digest()`. `concat`, `hmac`, and `none` are the alternatives; an unknown string raises `TypeError` only when `derive_key` is first called, not at construction.","The salt enters the signature only through this derived key, so two serializers with the same secret and different salts produce signatures that will never validate for each other.","Because `salt` and `secret_key` are concatenated without a separator, distinct (salt, key) pairs can in principle collide into the same derived key — a reason to keep salts fixed constants rather than user input.","The default digest is `_lazy_sha1`, a wrapper that defers touching `hashlib.sha1` until call time so FIPS builds without SHA-1 can be reconfigured before first use instead of failing at import.","`HMACAlgorithm.get_signature` returns the raw HMAC digest; `Signer.get_signature` base64url-encodes it, giving the 27-character tail seen in the token."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q3.1","question":"SHA-1 is the documented default. Is signing on a broken hash something an owner should refuse to sign off on?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q1.1","answer":"The salt is mixed into the derived key, so it partitions signatures into contexts: an 'auth' token cannot be replayed against an 'activate' or 'upgrade' serializer sharing the same secret. It is a namespace, not a secret."}]},{"n":4,"title":"A Dot, and the Token Leaves the Building","trace_lines":[1,1],"data_in":"payload b'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9' and signature b'6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg'","data_out":"'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9.6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg' (str, printed as trace line 1)","code":["src/itsdangerous/signer.py:222-225","src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:314-320","src/itsdangerous/signer.py:144-151"],"inputs":["value=b'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9'"],"characters":["Signer.sign","Signer.sep","_base64_alphabet","Serializer.dumps"],"facts":["`sign` is literally `value + sep + signature`; the signature covers exactly the bytes to its left, and nothing else — not the salt string, not the serializer identity, except as they were folded into the derived key.","The constructor rejects any `sep` that appears in `_base64_alphabet` (ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `=`) with a `ValueError`, because a separator that can occur inside a signature would make the split ambiguous. The default `b\".\"` is outside that set. This is the road not taken here.","Because `is_text_serializer` is True, `dumps` decodes the signed bytes as UTF-8 and returns `str`; a binary serializer such as pickle would return `bytes` from the same method.","The token is self-contained: there is no server-side state, no nonce, and no expiry. Replay of a valid token is not prevented by this class — `URLSafeTimedSerializer` exists for the age check, and revocation remains the caller's problem."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q4.1","question":"The payload is base64 and the signature is base64, but the separator is a dot — and a compressed payload starts with a dot too. How does the reverse trip split this unambiguously?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":5,"title":"The Token Comes Back, and Is Split Apart","trace_lines":[1,2],"data_in":"'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9.6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg' arriving from the client","data_out":"value=b'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9', sig=b'6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg'","code":["src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:328-343","src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:287-307","src/itsdangerous/signer.py:244-256"],"inputs":["s='eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9.6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg'","salt=None"],"characters":["Serializer.loads","Serializer.iter_unsigners","Signer.unsign","BadSignature"],"facts":["`loads` normalizes the input with `want_bytes`, then loops over `iter_unsigners(salt)`, catching only `BadSignature`; if every signer rejects the token it re-raises the last exception.","`iter_unsigners` yields the primary signer first, then for each fallback entry (a dict of kwargs, a Signer class, or a (class, kwargs) tuple) one signer per secret key. With no fallbacks configured, exactly one signer is yielded here.","`unsign` first checks the separator is present at all and raises `BadSignature(\"No b'.' found in value\")` if not — the road not taken for a well-formed token.","The split is `rsplit(sep, 1)`: the *last* dot wins, so a leading dot marking a compressed payload stays on the value side and cannot be confused with the separator.","Nothing is deserialized before the signature is checked: `load_payload` is only reached with bytes that `unsign` returned, which is the ordering that makes a pickle-based serializer merely dangerous rather than immediately fatal."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q5.1","question":"Only one signer was tried. What does the loop buy when keys are being rotated or a digest is being upgraded?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q4.1","answer":"`unsign` uses `rsplit(sep, 1)`, splitting on the final dot only. A compression-marking leading dot is therefore part of the value, and `load_payload` strips it after verification."}]},{"n":6,"title":"Constant Time, Newest Key First","trace_lines":[1,2],"data_in":"value=b'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9', sig=b'6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg'","data_out":"True — and `unsign` returns the value bytes","code":["src/itsdangerous/signer.py:227-242","src/itsdangerous/signer.py:24-28","src/itsdangerous/encoding.py:28-38","src/itsdangerous/signer.py:31-37"],"inputs":["sig=b'6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg'"],"characters":["Signer.verify_signature","SigningAlgorithm.verify_signature","hmac.compare_digest","base64_decode","NoneAlgorithm"],"facts":["The comparison is `hmac.compare_digest(sig, expected)`, which is constant-time with respect to content, removing the timing oracle a naive `==` would create.","Verification recomputes the expected signature rather than decrypting anything; an attacker without the secret cannot produce a matching tag for modified bytes.","Keys are tried `reversed(self.secret_keys)` — newest first — so the common case costs one HMAC and rotated-out keys only cost extra work for stale tokens.","A signature that is not valid base64 is caught by the bare `except Exception` around `base64_decode` and turned into `return False`, not an error type the caller must handle separately.","`NoneAlgorithm` exists and returns an empty signature; it is opt-in only. Choosing it, or `key_derivation=\"none\"`, disables the guarantee entirely, and neither is reachable by accident from the defaults used here."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q3.1","answer":"SHA-1's collision weakness does not transfer to its use as the inner hash of HMAC — even MD5 remains secure in HMAC. The default is documented and defensible; a project that still wants SHA-512 sets `signer_kwargs={\"digest_method\": hashlib.sha512}` and keeps SHA-1 in `fallback_signers` so old tokens survive the change."},{"id":"q5.1","answer":"The loop is the rotation and upgrade mechanism: `secret_keys` is tried newest-to-oldest inside one signer, and `fallback_signers` adds whole alternative signer configurations. Old tokens keep validating while new ones are issued under the new parameters."}]},{"n":7,"title":"Back to a Dict","trace_lines":[2,2],"data_in":"b'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9' (verified bytes)","data_out":"{'id': 5, 'name': 'itsdangerous'} — `data[\"name\"]` printed as trace line 2","code":["src/itsdangerous/url_safe.py:23-53","src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:243-269","src/itsdangerous/encoding.py:28-38","src/itsdangerous/_json.py:10-12"],"inputs":["payload=b'eyJpZCI6NSwibmFtZSI6Iml0c2Rhbmdlcm91cyJ9'"],"characters":["URLSafeSerializerMixin.load_payload","Serializer.load_payload","base64_decode","zlib.decompress","BadPayload"],"facts":["The payload does not start with `b\".\"`, so `decompress` stays False and `zlib.decompress` is never called — the road not taken for this token.","`base64_decode` re-adds the stripped `=` padding and decodes with `errors=\"ignore\"` on the ASCII step; invalid base64 raises `BadData`, which the mixin re-wraps as `BadPayload`.","A failed `zlib.decompress` is likewise wrapped in `BadPayload` with the original exception attached, so a decompression bomb or garbage compressed block surfaces as a library error rather than a zlib traceback — though size of the decompressed output is not bounded by this code.","`Serializer.load_payload` decodes UTF-8 before calling the serializer because `is_text_serializer` is True, and wraps any exception from `serializer.loads` in `BadPayload` with `original_error` preserved.","Round trip complete: the dict equals the original, which is the guarantee the whole stack exists to provide — the data came back unchanged or not at all."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q7.1","question":"`BadPayload` is raised here, after the signature already passed. Does `loads` catch it like it catches `BadSignature`?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q2.1","answer":"Nothing stops a client from prepending a dot — and that is fine, because `load_payload` runs only after `unsign` has verified the bytes. A forged dot changes the signed value and fails verification before zlib is ever reached."}]},{"n":8,"title":"The Forged Twin","trace_lines":[3,4],"data_in":"'eyJpZCI6MSwibmFtZSI6ImFkbWluIn0.6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg' — a genuine signature glued to an attacker's payload claiming id 1, name admin","data_out":"BadSignature: Signature b'6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg' does not match (trace line 3); the run ends normally at line 4","code":["src/itsdangerous/signer.py:244-256","src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:328-343","src/itsdangerous/exc.py:7-33","src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:349-395"],"inputs":["s='eyJpZCI6MSwibmFtZSI6ImFkbWluIn0.6YP6T0BaO67XP--9UzTrmurXSmg'"],"characters":["Signer.unsign","Serializer.loads","BadSignature","BadPayload","Serializer.loads_unsafe"],"facts":["`verify_signature` returns False for the swapped payload, so `unsign` raises `BadSignature(f\"Signature {sig!r} does not match\", payload=value)` — the message quotes the *signature*, and the rejected payload bytes are attached, not discarded.","`loads` stores that exception as `last_exception`, finds no further signers, and re-raises it; the caller sees one `BadSignature` regardless of how many keys or fallbacks were tried, with no indication of which failed.","`e.payload` is deliberately exposed so callers can inspect tampered data, but it is untrusted by construction; `docs/serializer.rst` and `loads_unsafe` both warn that decoding it is an explicit, separate decision.","`loads` catches only `BadSignature`. `BadPayload` is a sibling under `BadData`, so a payload that verifies but fails to deserialize propagates immediately and is never retried against another signer — callers that only catch `BadSignature` will see it escape.","What the code guarantees, end to end: a token that `loads` returns was produced by a holder of one of the configured secret keys under the same salt and signer parameters. What it does not guarantee: secrecy of the payload, freshness, single use, revocation, or any bound on payload size.","Known misuse shapes to ask about in review: a secret key committed to source or shared across environments, a shared or user-controlled salt, a non-JSON `serializer` such as pickle combined with `loads_unsafe` or manual `load_payload` on `e.payload`, and treating `URLSafeSerializer` as if it expired tokens when `URLSafeTimedSerializer` with `max_age` is what does that."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q7.1","answer":"No. `loads` catches `BadSignature` only; `BadPayload` descends from `BadData` alongside it and propagates straight to the caller, skipping any remaining fallback signers."}]}]}
